text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan sees no change in its old relationship with China that transcends political, regional or ideological changes.
- The Pakistan Muslim League (Junejo group), an ally of the Pakistan People's Party, has split into two factions.

- The Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture has informed the interim cabinet that Pakistan may have to import a record 2.4 millions tonnes of wheat in 1997/98 (July-June), which is 25 percent more than the current year.
- The Asian Development Bank has approved a $200 million interest-free loan to help women and children in rural Pakistan.
- About 32,674 metric tonnes of soyabean seeds, costing about $10 million, have arrived at the Port Qasim from the United States under its concesssional loan agreement.
- The government has finalised measures to bail out the National Investment Trust, which faces a liquidity crunch.
- Pakistani rice export prices are likely to remain steady next week amid low foreign demand.
- The Privatisation Commission plans to fetch $1.0 billion through placement of ten global depositary receipts (GDRs) during the next 12 months.
- The Privatisation Commission has decided to initiate strong legal action against defaulters of 2.82 billion rupees, said Commission's Chairman Salman Shah.
- The government is contemplating short-term measures to check the unprecedented financial and resource crisis faced by Pakistan, and making plans for long-term economic growth.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid said the government had intitiated the accountability process under which large- scale arrests were expected in a few days.
- Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah said the Supreme Court would try to decide the petititons filed against the National Assembly (lower house) dissolution in the shortest possible time.
- Petroleum and Natural Resources Minister Javed Jabbar said the government will review oil prices every month.
